title: Data Privacy Maze
instructions: Decide whether the data request is safe or suspicious.

questions.question: A quiz website asks for your birthday and home address.
questions.hint: Sites should not require personal info for quizzes.

questions.question: An app asks location only while in use.
questions.hint: Minimal permissions = acceptable.

questions.question: A random website asks for your home address to continue.
questions.hint: Websites rarely need physical addresses.

questions.question: An app requests access to your camera only when taking a picture.
questions.hint: Contextual camera access is normal.

questions.question: A mobile game asks for your contact list for no clear reason.
questions.hint: Games rarely need contact access.

questions.question: A shopping website asks for your phone number only during checkout.
questions.hint: Used for delivery and updates.

questions.question: A free WiFi network requires your email and full date of birth.
questions.hint: DOB is sensitive personal data.

questions.question: A browser extension wants access to 'read your browsing history'.
questions.hint: Be cautious with extensions requesting excessive permissions.

questions.question: A food delivery app asks for your delivery address to complete an order.
questions.hint: Necessary for delivery.

questions.question: A random quiz website asks for your full name and phone number.
questions.hint: Quizzes should not need personal details.

questions.question: An app asks for microphone access but only when recording audio.
questions.hint: On-demand access is acceptable.

questions.question: A VPN app requests access to your location for no reason.
questions.hint: VPN services do not need location.

questions.question: A flashlight app wants access to your photos and media files.
questions.hint: Permissions unrelated to app function are risky.

questions.question: A website asks you to allow browser notifications.
questions.hint: Safe if you trust the website.

questions.question: An e-commerce website asks you to save your card details for faster checkout.
questions.hint: Safe only on reputable, secure platforms.

questions.question: A mobile app asks for your location even when not in use.
questions.hint: Unnecessary background location is dangerous.

questions.question: A banking app asks permission to read SMS for OTP auto-detection.
questions.hint: Standard practice for secure apps.

questions.question: A job portal asks for your resume but also requests your Aadhaar number.
questions.hint: Government IDs shouldn't be shared with portals.

questions.question: A fitness app asks for your health data to track progress.
questions.hint: Health apps require such information.

questions.question: An unknown Chrome extension asks to 'read and change all your data on all websites'.
questions.hint: These permissions can capture sensitive data.

questions.question: Your college portal asks for your student ID and date of birth to reset password.
questions.hint: Common identity verification process.

questions.question: An app promises prize money for sharing your full name and contact list.
questions.hint: Data-harvesting scams often offer rewards.

questions.question: A messaging app wants access to your media files to store sent photos.
questions.hint: Messaging apps do need media access.

questions.question: A research survey requires your location to match region-based trends.
questions.hint: Reasonable for location-based studies.

questions.question: A website insists that disabling ad-blockers is mandatory to access content.
questions.hint: Aggressive access requirements can indicate tracking.

questions.question: A random email link asks you to re-enter your saved passwords.
questions.hint: Credible sites never ask to re-enter saved passwords.

questions.question: A social media app requests contact access to find friends but explains how it'll be used.
questions.hint: Transparency is key to trusting permissions.

questions.question: A free wallpaper app requests access to your location and microphone.
questions.hint: Unrelated permissions = privacy risk.

questions.question: A government website asks for your PAN for tax filing.
questions.hint: Government portals require identity data.

questions.question: A shopping app requests camera access for barcode scanning.
questions.hint: Feature-related permission.

questions.question: A free game asks you to enable full device access to improve performance.
questions.hint: Games should not require deep system access.

questions.question: An email instructs you to upload your ID picture to verify an unfamiliar account.
questions.hint: Never upload ID for unknown accounts.

questions.question: A browser extension for screenshots asks permission to "read and change data on all websites".
questions.hint: Unnecessary global permissions can capture private data.

questions.question: A weather app asks for your approximate location to show local forecasts.
questions.hint: Weather apps need location for relevant updates.

questions.question: A shopping mall WiFi login page requires your full name, phone number, and date of birth.
questions.hint: Public WiFi should not need detailed personal data.

questions.question: Your bank’s website asks for your PAN while updating KYC information.
questions.hint: KYC legally requires identity proof.

questions.question: A gaming app asks for access to your device’s location even when the app is closed.
questions.hint: Background location tracking is a major privacy red flag.

questions.question: A professional networking site asks you to upload a resume containing contact details.
questions.hint: Expected for job portals.

questions.question: An unknown survey link asks for your photos 'for identity verification'.
questions.hint: Identity verification is NOT done via random surveys.

questions.question: A yoga app asks for height, weight, and age to generate your workout plan.
questions.hint: Fitness apps often require health details.

questions.question: Your phone warns: 'This app continuously accesses your microphone in the background.'
questions.hint: Background mic access is highly suspicious.

questions.question: A school portal requests parents' phone numbers for emergency contact details.
questions.hint: Necessary for safety and communication.

questions.question: A fan website asks you to enter your Aadhaar number to participate in a contest.
questions.hint: Never provide government ID for contests.

questions.question: Your browser warns that a website is trying to track your precise location.
questions.hint: Precise location is highly sensitive.

questions.question: A website requests permission to store cookies related to user preference settings.
questions.hint: Preference cookies are normal.

questions.question: A free horoscope site asks for your full name, date of birth, and birth time.
questions.hint: DOB + name combination is very sensitive data.

questions.question: A mobile app requests access to Bluetooth for connecting a smartwatch.
questions.hint: Device pairing requires Bluetooth access.

questions.question: A random website asks to track your activity across other websites.
questions.hint: Cross-site tracking = privacy invasion.

questions.question: An app asks for NFC access to enable tap-to-pay features.
questions.hint: Required for digital payments.

questions.question: You receive an SMS link asking to update your digital wallet credentials.
questions.hint: Never update credentials via SMS links.

questions.question: A travel booking site requests passport information while booking an international flight.
questions.hint: Mandatory for international travel.

questions.question: A free theme app asks for permission to 'display over other apps'.
questions.hint: Overlay permissions can be abused for attack.

questions.question: A medical appointment app requests health details and history.
questions.hint: Medical apps need accurate health information.

questions.question: Your phone warns: 'This app is accessing location too frequently.'
questions.hint: Excess location access = privacy issue.

questions.question: A random store asks for your phone number for 'exclusive offers'.
questions.hint: Avoid sharing phone numbers unnecessarily.

questions.question: An app wants access to your clipboard to 'offer smarter suggestions'.
questions.hint: Clipboard access can expose passwords or OTPs.

questions.question: A shopping app reads your SMS to auto-detect OTP for payments.
questions.hint: Secure payment apps do this legitimately.

questions.question: A browser warns that a website is trying to download multiple files automatically.
questions.hint: Bulk automatic downloads are a red flag.

questions.question: A random Telegram channel link asks you to enter your phone number to join.
questions.hint: Official join links never ask for phone numbers.

questions.question: A game requests camera access to place AR (augmented reality) characters.
questions.hint: AR games require camera access.

questions.question: A survey website requires your email before allowing participation and explains why.
questions.hint: Transparency improves trust.

questions.question: You get a request to sync your phone contacts to an unknown social media app.
questions.hint: Avoid sharing contacts with untrusted apps.

questions.question: A new social media app asks for access to your SMS messages to 'verify your identity'.
questions.hint: Identity verification does not require full SMS access.

questions.question: Your university portal asks for your admission number and date of birth to view grades.
questions.hint: Common information required in academic portals.

questions.question: An unknown health app wants access to your camera, microphone, location, and contact list on installation.
questions.hint: Too many permissions without explanation = red flag.

questions.question: A delivery service app asks for your location to find your nearest delivery address.
questions.hint: Expected functionality for such apps.

questions.question: A streaming service requests access to your device storage to download movies offline.
questions.hint: Required to store offline files.

questions.question: An app wants permission to track your location across all apps for 'personalized ads'.
questions.hint: Cross-app tracking is invasive.

questions.question: A website asks you to confirm your phone number to receive a one-time password for signup.
questions.hint: OTP verification is typical for new accounts.

questions.question: A random online store wants permission to access all your saved passwords.
questions.hint: Legitimate websites never request saved passwords.

questions.question: Your email provider requests alternate phone number for recovery purposes.
questions.hint: Backup recovery options are standard.

questions.question: A popular shopping app asks to track your activity across other apps for analytics.
questions.hint: Cross-app activity tracking is highly sensitive.

questions.question: A PDF viewer app requests access to your contacts for 'sharing features', even though in-app sharing exists.
questions.hint: Unnecessary access to contacts = privacy risk.

questions.question: An established bank app asks to access your phone’s call logs for enhanced fraud detection.
questions.hint: Call logs are never needed for banking.

questions.question: A shopping website asks to store cookies for maintaining items in your cart.
questions.hint: Functional cookies are necessary for e-commerce.

questions.question: Your email inbox warns that an external app is requesting full access to read and delete your emails.
questions.hint: Full access is rarely needed and very risky.

questions.question: A health portal asks you to upload medical prescriptions for teleconsultation.
questions.hint: Medical apps require data to offer services.

questions.question: A game without online features requests access to your network activity logs.
questions.hint: Offline games should not track network activity.

questions.question: Your ISP requests your alternate phone number for service outages and notifications.
questions.hint: Used for service communication.

questions.question: A shopping website asks for your credit card CVV via email due to 'billing problems'.
questions.hint: Never share CVV outside secure payment portals.

questions.question: Your phone warns that a newly installed app is accessing your clipboard in the background.
questions.hint: Clipboard spying is dangerous.

questions.question: A travel app requests permission to access your email inbox to 'check for booked tickets'.
questions.hint: Apps should not scan your inbox.

questions.question: A fake government portal requests your biometric fingerprints for 'identity validation'.
questions.hint: Never share biometrics outside official channels.

questions.question: A malicious browser extension claims to offer cashback but requests access to all your online transactions.
questions.hint: Some extensions steal financial data.

questions.question: An app insists on enabling screen recording permissions to 'improve user experience'.
questions.hint: Screen capture permissions can expose passwords, chats, and OTPs.

questions.question: A fraudulent loan application website requires your bank account number, IFSC, and full login password.
questions.hint: Never enter your login password anywhere except official portals.

questions.question: Your organization receives a phishing email asking employees to upload ID cards to an external drive link.
questions.hint: ID collection phishing targets companies.

questions.question: A malicious app requests permission to modify system settings on your device.
questions.hint: System settings access is dangerous unless necessary.

questions.question: A fake e-wallet verification page asks you to share a selfie with your ID card.
questions.hint: Attackers use identity theft through fake verification.

questions.question: A seemingly harmless extension captures keystrokes to provide 'typing analytics'.
questions.hint: Keystroke access = keylogger behavior.

questions.question: An app asks for root access on your phone to unlock premium features.
questions.hint: Root access exposes full system data.

questions.question: A cyber-attack uses a fake browser update pop-up to take full device control.
questions.hint: Fake updates are used for malware delivery.

questions.question: A caller pretends to be your bank manager and demands your ATM PIN urgently.
questions.hint: Banks NEVER ask for PINs.

questions.question: Your boss emails you from an unknown Gmail account asking for vouchers.
questions.hint: Leaders don't use personal emails for urgent money requests.

questions.question: A friend suddenly texts from a new number asking for money without calling.
questions.hint: Always verify identity with a call.

questions.question: A courier calls asking for an OTP to deliver your package.
questions.hint: Couriers never ask for OTPs.

questions.question: A charity worker pressures you to donate immediately at your doorstep.
questions.hint: Pressure = social engineering.

questions.question: An email claims you won a lottery you never entered.
questions.hint: No participation = no prize.

questions.question: Someone you don't know asks for your office WiFi password 'just for one minute'.
questions.hint: Never share network credentials.

questions.question: A stranger on social media asks for your personal number.
questions.hint: Social engineers build trust to steal data.

questions.question: A caller says they're from 'IT support' and wants remote access to your computer.
questions.hint: Remote access requests are suspicious.

questions.question: Someone offers a too-good-to-be-true job if you pay a small 'verification fee'.
questions.hint: Real jobs never charge fees.

questions.question: A coworker asks for your system login because 'his machine isn’t working'.
questions.hint: Credentials should never be shared.

questions.question: An SMS claims to be from your bank but uses a shortened URL.
questions.hint: Short links hide malicious sites.

questions.question: Someone tailgates behind you into an office building claiming their ID card is lost.
questions.hint: Tailgating is a physical social engineering tactic.

questions.question: Your 'bank' asks you to verify account details over a call at odd hours.
questions.hint: Banks follow strict timing and procedures.

questions.question: During onboarding, HR asks for official documents through a verified company portal.
questions.hint: Valid HR processes use secure portals.

questions.question: A stranger claims to be a technician and wants access to your office desk.
questions.hint: Always verify visitor identity.

questions.question: A fake recruiter offers a high salary but asks for your Aadhaar and PAN immediately.
questions.hint: Identity theft risks.

questions.question: A coworker sends a message from an unknown number requesting project files.
questions.hint: Identity must be verified on the official channel.

questions.question: Someone impersonates a courier and asks to sign a digital pad requiring unnecessary details.
questions.hint: Excessive data during delivery = scam.

questions.question: Your electricity provider requests your meter number and account ID via their official app.
questions.hint: Official apps are legitimate channels.

questions.question: A scammer pretends to be your relative stuck in an emergency abroad.
questions.hint: Classic social engineering emotional manipulation.

questions.question: Someone online gains trust over weeks and asks for private photos.
questions.hint: Long-term manipulation is grooming.

questions.question: A fake LinkedIn profile messages you asking for your corporate email.
questions.hint: Attackers use fake profiles to gather credentials.

questions.question: A colleague asks you to open a USB drive found in the parking lot.
questions.hint: USB drops are used for malware attacks.

questions.question: A job application website asks for basic details and clearly states why each one is needed.
questions.hint: Transparency indicates legitimacy.

questions.question: A stranger asks you to forward a confidential company document to help them apply for a job.
questions.hint: Confidential documents must not be shared.

questions.question: You receive a fake tech support popup claiming your system is infected.
questions.hint: Scare tactics drive social engineering scams.

questions.question: A stranger in your office building wears no ID badge but claims to be new.
questions.hint: Unauthorized presence is suspicious.

questions.question: Your bank calls but asks you to provide last 4 digits of your account for confirmation.
questions.hint: Banks may request partial verification data.

questions.question: A scammer pretends to be from customer care and demands remote access to fix an issue.
questions.hint: Remote access = malware risk.
